prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” lawyer for every truck-accident case — the right lawyer depends on the facts of your crash, the injuries, the attorney’s experience with trucking cases, and how well you work with them. That said, here’s a practical way to find the best personal-injury lawyer in Dallas for your truck accident:

What to look for
- Trucking-specific experience: look for attorneys who regularly handle commercial vehicle and truck-accident cases (not just general personal injury).
- Trial experience: trucking companies and insurers often only settle for the right pressure—make sure the attorney will try the case if necessary.
- Resources: cases involving trucks commonly require accident reconstructionists, electronic data (“black box”) retrieval, medical experts, and investigation of logbooks and maintenance records.
- Track record: settlements and verdicts in truck cases, plus client testimonials and peer recognition (Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, AVVO, Martindale‑Hubbell).
- Board certification or memberships: Texas Board of Legal Specialization (civil trial), Dallas Trial Lawyers Association, Texas Trial Lawyers Association.
- Communication and accessibility: clear fee structure (usually contingency), responsiveness, and a written retainer agreement.

Key practical points
- Statute of limitations in Texas for most personal-injury claims is 2 years from the crash (there are special rules for suits vs. governmental entities). Act promptly.
- Truck cases can involve federal regulations (FMCSA), multiple defendants (driver, trucking company, motor carrier, owner, maintenance provider), and large insurers—pick a lawyer who knows these issues.
- Most good truck-accident lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover).

Where to look
- Search Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Martindale‑Hubbell, AVVO for Dallas truck-accident or commercial-vehicle specialists.
- Ask local referrals: doctors, other lawyers, or people in support groups who’ve had similar cases.
- Local legal organizations: Dallas Trial Lawyers Association.

Questions to ask at a free consult
- How many truck-accident cases have you handled in Dallas? How many in the last 3 years?
- Do you have trial experience in truck cases? Can you provide recent verdicts/settlements?
- What resources and experts would you use?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- Do you take cases on contingency? What percentage and what costs will I pay if there’s a recovery?
- How long will you expect my case to take?
- Will you retain my medical records and bills, or do I handle that?

If you’d like, I can:
- Narrow down a short list of Dallas lawyers/firms known for truck cases (I’ll need your ZIP or neighborhood),
- Draft a message or set of questions to send when you contact firms,
- Help you evaluate responses from attorneys you’ve already spoken with.

Which of those would you like me to do next?
